title: Engram control admission stays within its dispatch budget while a full gate runs on the same host
outcome: Under the load of a full gate's Rust test stage on the same machine, Engram's control admission (evaluate, fence, begin) answers TermAl's turn_begin within its dispatch budget, so turns are not withheld and queues are not paused; or the record shows by measurement that the latency is outside Engram, cross-referenced to the TermAl item.
acceptance: The 2026-10-21 04:31-04:35Z stall (dispatch_budget_exhausted at 04:31:48Z and 04:32:31Z, then begin_preparation_pending at 04:33:19Z; evaluate 9.8-19.8 s, fence 7.2-13.3 s; Greg reports 21-30 s) is attributed by measurement to its phases (store open, SQLite lock or busy wait, query and projection work, fsync or WAL checkpoint, response) and to the contended resource (disk I/O, CPU, SQLite lock), or the record names the evidence gap
A reproduction runs a full-gate Rust test stage, or an equivalent measured load, beside repeated admissions and shows whether admission latency exceeds the dispatch budget under that load

Either an in-scope Engram defect is fixed with a test that reproduces the slow path and shows admission back within budget under the load, or the record concludes with evidence that the cause is outside Engram, with a cross-reference to the TermAl item for the UX side (automatic recovery shown as blocking cards and a paused queue)
disposal_reason: Obsolete on Greg's word (Asistant #239): the evaluate, fence and begin admission path and its dispatch budget no longer exist. A store-latency problem under gate load would be its own item with current evidence.
